videos.title: Inside China’s Race To Build The World’s Data Centers
videos.description:
Chinese companies are using prefabricated construction to build data centers faster and more efficiently. As America’s AI-driven data center boom accelerates, China’s BrightRay hopes to win U.S. business with its modular approach. But growing U.S.-China tensions, national-security concerns and restrictions on some Chinese-made products could limit that opportunity. CNBC's China Bureau Chief Eunice Yoon reports.

videos.title: Inside Texas's Growing Political Fight Over Data Centers
videos.description:
Texas has long attracted data centers with its pro-business policies and abundance of land. Today, it’s one of the biggest data center hubs in the country, but residents are starting to push back over issues like transparency, water use and power bills. CNBC traveled to Texas to learn how the growing backlash has made data centers a key issue in the upcoming race between Ken Paxton and James Talarico–and in midterm elections across the country.

Reporter: Justin Papp
Produced and Shot by: Macklin Fishman
Edited by: Andrea Miller
Animation: Emily Park, Jason Reginato
Additional Camera: Andrew Evers
Additional Editing: Rowan Buck, Christian Nunley

videos.title: Exclusive: Ride-Along Inside Aurora’s Self-Driving Semitruck
videos.description:

CNBC's Phil LeBeau spoke with Aurora CEO Chris Urmson to learn more about why he believes autonomous freight is nearing a turning point.

videos.title: How Williams-Sonoma Became One Of Retail’s Best-Performing Stocks
videos.description:
Williams-Sonoma is outperforming the home furnishing industry and broader market. The company is increasingly able to sell products with minimal discounting, grow business-to-business sales and integrate AI to grow its market share. CNBC’s Ryan Baker explains how the home goods company has been able to grow profitability despite a stagnant housing market, economic uncertainty and tariff pressures.

videos.title: Why It’s So Hard To Build An AI Kill Switch
videos.description:
AI doomerism hit a fever pitch after former OpenAI and Anthropic researchers warned that AI could kill us, and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, OpenAI's Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk joined the cause. As runaway AI fears reached a crescendo, policymakers renewed calls for a magic stop button for AI or a kill switch, which would require model makers to build a capability to shut down access when an agents go awry. CNBC speaks to experts to find out what it would take to build an AI kill switch.

videos.title: ‘Concerned:’ Samsung, Micron And Other Chipmakers Face U.S. Worker Shortage
videos.description:
Manpower is key for making enough chips to power AI, but a new report shows the U.S. faces a shortage of up to 157,000 semiconductor workers by 2030. Samsung sits down for a rare interview with CNBC's Katie Tarasov about why it's "concerned" as it prepares to open a new logic fab in Texas, within months of other U.S. fabs coming online from TSMC, Intel, Micron and SK Hynix. For now, U.S. chipmakers like Micron hold hiring sprees in Asia, which has dominating the industry for decades and offers chip jobs with bonuses upwards of $500,000. CNBC finds out what chipmakers and U.S. schools like Purdue and Arizona State University are doing to entice the next generation of U.S. students to study chip engineering, in hopes of creating a talent pipeline that will keep from crippling U.S. ambitions to lead in AI.

0:00 Introduction
2:28 Chip manufacturing in the U.S.
4:47 Front-end fabs, thousands of workers
7:44 Creating the pipeline

videos.title: Inside Bracket22, A Trading Firm Powered By Al Agents
videos.description:
Brian Kelly previously ran a cryptocurrency hedge fund, but closed that shop in early 2025. Later that year, he began testing out uses of artificial intelligence. Bracket22 invests only Kelly's own capital and trades cryptocurrencies, stocks and commodities. It's powered entirely by AI agents — a stark example of a growing reality on Wall Street as firms test the benefits and limits of AI in finance.
